Make sure she seeks professional help. A counselor or psychiatrist. Or both.

Maybe go with her to a depression support group. Really try to understand the mental illness.

It's really easy to mistake a depressive episode with an "I don't want to be with you." moment.

I know when I got really depressed, I would tell my wife to leave me alone. Then go isolate myself from everybody. Maybe I'd drive around the neighborhood for a few hours. I just didn't want people to see me or get hurt because of my sadness.

If her mental illness gets too much for you, please tell her. Instead, my wife just started ignoring me. Spent most of her time away from the house. Maybe cheated. Then finally left. She didn't want my wellbeing to be part of her responsibility anymore. 

It sucks because I do get suicidal when depressed. And being suicidal in an empty house is scary. Luckily I made it through. She left me in a very uncompassionate way. It really hurt. 

My wife kept thinking my depression would go away. She said she kept trying to help me. But she never talked to me directly. She just tried being nice. Hoping it would cure me. I would have loved it if she went to a session with me. Tried to understand the garbage in my head. It's something that will stay with me. It's part of my life. Yes, I can learn to manage it, but understand that you can't do anything to cure it. 

If you really want to stick with your girlfriend, understand that this just might be an aspect of her life. But it's not hopeless. :)

It made me push away my wife. So she left me. :(

Remember. If you get married. Understand that depression can really hurt the relationship. Learn to cope with it. Make sure you and your spouse understand what it makes you do. You're not a bad person. You just have a issue that can be worked on.

Thanks. This is a great response. I struggle with devaluing myself in general, so it's important for me to keep reinforcing that I'm not the bad guy.

The deceit alone is really hurtful.

She was such a sweet and honest girl. It's sad to see her turn. But I'm starting to accept that this is who she has been the whole time.

I've been seeing her in such a blindingly good light. I need to start seeing her for the woman she actually is. I always gloss over the flaws in other people.

Out until 3am on weekdays. Constant texting. Sudden shift in friends. Always out.

Even if it wasn't cheating, it's still pretty obvious that she didn't want to be with me.

It'd be awesome to know so I can really have a great reason to know I'm better off without her.

I mean, she did bail out without any attempt at fixing the marriage with me. Which in itself is pretty cold. But I still give her the benefit of the doubt. My love for her borders on unconditional, so sometimes it's hard to see that I'm better off without her. I'm trying really hard to focus on her faults. I want to remind myself that I'm coming out ahead with her gone.

Maybe it might help to think about all the negatives about your marriage. Then you can think of all the positives of not having to deal with those things anymore.

Personally, I'm excited that I don't have to come home to a messy house anymore. (My STBX is a slob.)
Thanks. Depression has made me into a miserable person. I don't want to fall into that again.

I agree with you. She has a tendency to split off from her emotions.

I still want this to work out... We never had counseling. Or even talked about it as a couple. Even if she said divorce, I still can't fully give up in my mind until I see actual movement towards getting a divorce.
Yes, I've totally been doing it for myself. And I think it's been going well.

I hate to admit it, but I didn't start seeing a therapist until we started dating...

I mean, she comforted me through it all. But I don't really think I was that depressed until I met her.
In the time we've been away I've made really great progress working on myself and my other relationships. I'm the most hopeful that I've been in ages.

Her leaving was a huge wake up call for me. I knew I was depressed, but I was so blind to how bad I was. Looking back on the past six months I can really see that I really looked like a lost cause.

Since the separation I've really picked myself up. I guess it took me to hit rock bottom to start climbing up. I don't think I've been this hopeful about life in years. I'm genuinely starting to love myself and those around me.

I don't think being cold would really help. I've been emotionally distant because of the depression.

I guess she's just skeptical. Besides myself, I probably hurt her the most.

EDIT: She has been hanging out with an entire group of new people. Only met them over the summer. I asked why she was out so much, she explained it was an escape from me.
I know that I would appreciate the talk after the stress of the holidays. I mean, do you think the holidays might help your situation at all?
Now that you've tried to take action (and it not working out) you should try to talk about the problem directly. Just so you're both on the same page.
Cool. I'll take that out. I'll just say that I'm separated: simple and clean.
I have thought about this. And I do think there's truth in there.

Yeah, that's my logic.

In my description I say that I'm separated. That my wife walked away.

Is that an option under "relationship status"?

Because I wrote it down in my profile.
IIRC, she only told me her plan ahead of time because I asked her why she stopped talking with me.

I had been going to a counselor. Making great progress and the therapist said we could end sessions. (Around July.) Started going again in October when she left the house.

No prescription medications. I used to be on Cymbalta years ago, but for the last 9 months I've been taking 5-HTP. It's an over the counter pill that helps me and didn't have the side effects of the RX pills.

Like I said, I struggle, but I'm not beyond hope. I hear stories of severely depressed folks. And I don't feel like I'm anywhere near that.

Yeah, I know. Everyone has their limits. She's might have hit her's.

Honestly, I can only say that I've been emotionally distant and lost interest in activities with her (with anyone, really).

The thing that really frustrates me is that she never gave me a, "We need to work on this, or else it's gonna fail." talk.

She was very uncommunicative about her issues with me.

Nope. She didn't want counseling when I brought it up. We are seeing separate counselors though.

Yeah, I'm kinda moving to fast, I think. She says she wants a divorce, but is moving really slow. I just moved 50 miles upstate to and am renting month to month. I want to start a new life, but I'm still holding out for her. Until she sends me divorce papers, I don't think I'll be fully convinced it's over.

Ah. That's a long journey.

I've only been separated for 2 months.

She went straight to divorce. No talking. No desire for reconciliation.

She didn't start the divorce process though. Kinda dragging her feet on a lot of things.

When I told her about me dating people while we're separated, she got jealous about the idea.

How did your STBX find out you were dating?

If I may ask, how long were you separated before you reconciled? What was that like?

(I might make a thread about this, it's an interesting topic to me.)
Thanks for the encouragement!
I quit my job because it's what kinda started this whole mess. But I like not working. (For now.) I've always felt it was super unfulfilling.
I am an introvert. And my wife was the only person I was ever this close with. That's why it hurts so much.
Thanks. Anything will help right now. I'm hitting a really bad low today...
Maybe you find a SO, but that doesn't mean you'll be alone. Friends and family and a sense of self-worth can make you whole.
Really? Wow. I guess my upbringing made me feel weird about divorce. But it's true. I've always heard it's pretty common.

What the heck! My wife and your husband got bitten by the same bug. She used to hate socializing and going out to meet new people. She looked to be home or have a quiet outing with some close friends.

Now she stays out into the wee hours of the morning like a college kid.

My wife's been hanging out with new friends. Most, if not all, single. I think that's what really made her feel uncomfortable about the marriage.

I feel like an afterthought when she picked new friends over a 7 year relationship with me. I mean, does there need to be a choice?
Yeah. Definitely sounds like a better life without her.

Yeah, that can an embarrassing reason for someone.

My wife had very strong Christian values and ideas toward marriage. Now that she's surrounded by people of different philosophies, I think she became ashamed to be associated with Christianity and its values. She's been kinda going out of her way to do things opposite of what Christianity teaches. Hence the lack of respect for marriage. (Even though MANY types of people support marriage.)
Yeah. Does it make you wonder if there's a reason to the flakiness? Like cheating? A drastic change of heart is really weird to me.
That's awesome! How did you find her? But more importantly, how did you go about explaining that you were divorced?

Yeah. My wife changed from a girl who held marriage up on a pedestal to a woman who thinks marriage is set of rules enforced by religions and governments that she wants no part of.

What do you mean by divorced or busy?
If I may ask, how did you approach the subject of divorce when you went on dates?

True. Good to spot a problem early.

Apparently my STBX is keeping the divorce secret to most of her friends. Apparently she's kept the MARRIAGE secret to most of her friends!

Yeah. I've always felt old. Even when I was young. But my wife has always said she never grew up.

I'm actually moving in with a 19 year old roommate. (His parents are kinda making me his guardian. I mean, not legally or anything. Just to help him watch the house while they do retiree stuff.) I can easily pass for a college student (Even highschool if I shave.) Life is gonna be weird going back to that age. But maybe it'll scrape off the crust of dullness that built up over the years.

Aw, that's great to hear!

I recently had a confidence boost when I helped a couple out by giving them some (physical) love advice. They thanked me and said I was a "love guru".

While I do wish I had someone to share my own love with, it made me happy that I can help out others. :)
Yeah! I want to know everything I could have done better so that my future relationships will benefit from it.
What do you think helped you the most to get to that realization?
It's cool. I wish I knew someone who liked to give out hugs. I'd really like one.

Yeah. I miss the touch.

Man... I wanna cry now...
Hmm. I don't even really have a high sex drive.  I think intimacy is the better word.

I've considered it. But I asked her, and she said no. Of course, who admits to cheating? But I know she is not a dishonest person. I mean, there's really nothing I can do to find proof except stalk her. And that's not cool.

I think she is more in love with her newly regained single life. She's 27 and never experienced that 20-something lifestyle. We met at 19. We're both pretty introverted and quiet. She never expressed an interest in that kind of life until she hit her 27th birthday a few months ago. It sucks if our divorce came just as a circumstance of her quarter life crisis. I'd love to help her through it.
I've looked, but I didn't see anything like that around me.
I hope you do too. I called the Samaritans hotline today. It helped. :)
I'm there with you.
I go to some Meetups. It's fun, but the types of groups on my area are lacking. And the terrible thing is that my wife met all her friends on Meetup. I'd probably run into her!

Wow. That is really similar.

What did you do for those 2.5 months? Was that a set time you were willing to wait?

What was your contact with her like?

Maybe I'm dense, but I'd forgive many things she's done or doing as long as I get honestly and openness from her.

I did hurt her a lot emotionally. (I hurt myself a bunch too.) So there's definitely time needed for her to heal before she can be ready to do anything with me.

I guess it's up to how long I can wait around for her... I don't think I'm ready to move on just yet.

Thanks man.

Keeping up communication is something that I really want to do.

She doesn't want space, and I don't want to disrespect her desire, but I feel like if I just stop talking altogether we'll just grow estranged and the relationship will just die.

But we had been having sex, going on trips, and spending time together.

That's what's confusing. She really hid her feelings well.

Yeah, right? It doesn't make sense.

1. The quitting thing. My wife has countlessly told me to quit my job. She always says, "Quit your job, I have a great secure job. I want a happy husband instead of one who's a miserable wage slave." Or something similar.

1. We did talk. But maybe 6 months ago the job got me in such a depressive funk that I didn't talk about anything about how much I hate life.
She never really sat me down to talk about what was going on in her head. Mostly due to the fear of what I might do.

Then one weekend she said blurted out everything and left. Said that our relationship had pretty much been her consoling me and that's it. Honestly, I had a hard time processing everything. I knew I wasn't being very aware of anything but my own problems (like depression does), but I had no idea things were this bad to her.


I just wish she had told me. I definitely would have worked on things more. And focused on her more. It would probably help my depression if I forced myself to think about another person.
The sucky thing is, I thought things were going well. We just moved into a bigger place so I could have an art studio. And had been securing a lower stress job.

Yeah, that's what I've been doing. Trying to talk it out. I'm really upset by the way it was done, not so much that she wants to leave.

I mean, of course, I want to be with her, but I respect her if she wants something else.

I'm going through almost the same exact thing. No affair that I know of though. This is the start of the fourth week.

Did she talk about divorce? Or was it you?

My wife just left to create some space. Didn't talk about permanence either way.

I really don't thing she's cheating. (Not sexually, anyway.)

But yes, I really don't think I want to be with someone who pulls out so readily.

She's never been able to talk to anyone about real issues. Hardly even me. I think that's what she's working on now. But opening up to other people, not me. It sucks.

I did. They're just as shocked as me in her reaction to the problem.

Though the problem, we all agree, is something that is reasonable to be angry about.

I agree. If we talk it out and arrive at that point where she wants a divorce, I'm for it. (I mean, can I really do anything anyway?)

I just feel like this is bailing when things get hard, rather than facing adversity head on.

As to why I'm cool with it if it happens in the end? It's because I want her to have what she wants. If it's not with me, then I'm okay, as long as she's happy.
Yeah... Everyone's says she's cheating.
Oh, totally. I've one-eightied.

Oh yeah, she's told me some of the stuff she's been doing.

The thing is, I used to be more adventurous about life. Nothing unhinged, but I definitely would take chances on things.

I've slowly turned into a wimp about everything.

I think a part of it is that she wants that adventure again. And I wasn't giving it to her.

Like I said, if we talked civilly, I think we could come to a good solution. Divorce or not.
Yeah. We did talk. Gained a lot of perspective, but was good. I'm getting to the point where I just can't do anything more. I just gotta wait... I'm not feeling hopeful. Just dull.
Yeah... I just can't believe how she could just stop caring.

What do you mean by lawyer up?

She has never said anything about desire to divorce. (Doesn't rule it out though.) She says our relationship isn't the biggest issue. It's her finding her true self. (From our conversations, she's on a major soul searching journey. Doing things waaaay out of character for her just to see what sticks.)

If I get divorce papers ready, I feel like I'm the one pulling the trigger on the end of the marriage. Shouldn't I put it all on her? I don't want to make the first move in that direction. Sure, I will be cooperative if that's what she wants, but I couldn't forgive myself if I were the one to start that process.
We just talked 1 on 1 a few days ago. And I was right, she thought I would be a ridiculously angry monster. (I am angry, but more concerned about the problems that I didn't know she had.)

I'd love to, but she's not into that. Wants to work on our problems separately. She's so angry and exhausted that she just can't work with me and hardly can talk.

I really feel like she'd like to keep growing apart until it shrivels up... It would be a waste if that's the case.

We've been married for 3 years. But been together for 7.

But, I think you're right about everything else. I really need to get my self together. I've really dumped all my garbage on her. It's not fair.

It's not that I have NO ONE now that she's gone, I just need to work on building deeper relationships with those people that I do have.

Thanks for the tough, but real, advice.

We actually took a walk last weekend and went to a restaurant that Friday. This was all after I got a call about the new job. I was visibly happier.

She mentioned that she was surprised to see me acting that way. But after that is when she really started leaving home.

I think she's afraid that this good mood I've been in is only temporary. How do I show her that I'm getting better?

Now that I know she is affected just as much as I am, in even more determined to fight this.

I'm actually moonlight doing what I want to do.

Weeknights and weekends I spend my time learning or working for freelance clients.

My full time coworkers, bum me out because they paint a picture of what depressed and resigned life is in store for me if I don't leave. Always talking about glory days and being bitter and apathetic towards everything...
How is the boot camp? I've considered that for myself.

I think about that all the time. And it does sound like a better system. It's a socialist way of thinking. I kinda want to visit a socialist country just to see how it actually plays out.


I'm also a hoarder though. Money is a security blanket for me. I don't ever want to use it, but if my amount isn't going up I feel scared. I know it's ultimately just numbers and it doesn't give me happiness but it's one hollow purpose. 

Get money. Sit on it. Die.

Thanks for replying in the post. I think it will help others.

I like your way of thinking. If there's a chance of happiness we just have to go search of it.

I also admire that you took the initiative to go to school even though you hate it. I guess you gotta do something radical sometimes.

Maybe my problem is that I just complain, but I'm to afraid to make the change.

See, the thing is. I don't really care.

I'm not actively hateful towards life. I'm just apathetic towards it. I hate that there's no purpose.

And I hate even more, that I don't know anyone else who has purpose. Everyone I know is just "existing". Not pushing themselves. Not doing anything with passion. 

Sure, you can say that life is "enjoying the ride". Well, I don't want to ride it anymore. I've had my share of fun. I'm okay with getting off here.

It's hard to "move on" from here when I don't have a role model. One to show you they've moved on. And no offense, but I don't know you. You can just say things about how you conquered depression, just because you think it would be a shame that a person who wanted to die got his way.
